primitives.name: Top-25 Candidate Digestor
primitives.verbatim_quote: c) TOP-25 digest: the 25 highest-scored phase2 candidates with their score, title, arxiv id, and the scorer's one-line reason.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'C_i': 'candidate i with score S_i', 'T_i': 'title of candidate i', 'I_i': 'arXiv ID of candidate i', 'R_i': 'reason string for candidate i'}
primitives.assumptions: Scores are comparable and ranked strictly; reasons are descriptive and unique per candidate.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When tie-breaking by ID fails, digest order becomes ambiguous.

layer2.mapping: Top-25 digest mirrors GSI’s top-k query result structure, enabling retrieval of most relevant papers under current scoring.

This mirrors GSI's Bayesian updating framework, where prior beliefs are refined through likelihoods derived from artifact metadata. The funnel counter primitive formalizes this as a sequential reduction process, while the scoring rubric encodes a learned kernel over paper features. The top-25 digest acts as a posterior summary statistic, capturing the highest-value outcomes under the current model. Failure modes include misalignment between scoring rubric and domain relevance, or incorrect funnel counts due to artifact corruption.
